title: Canary Watchtower: continuous golden-set divergence alerting and explainable quarantine
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement: We observe intermittent quality regressions surfaced only in staged traffic (canary/shadow) that escape simple aggregate latency/error SLOs. Existing golden-set scorecards are run offline and used in ad-hoc gating, but they lack real-time sensitivity, cohort weighting, and explainable annotations that engineers can act on during a rollout.

Proposal: Implement 'Canary Watchtower' — a continuous divergence monitor that compares live canary + shadow responses against curated golden prompt sets and historical baselines, producing a cohort-weighted divergence score, per-prompt explainability annotations, and policy hooks for automated quarantine or rollback. This system is intended to operate at the orchestration boundary (rollout conductor) and the Console for visibility.

Key capabilities: 1) Streaming golden probe ingestion: unify offline golden sets and live synthetic probes into a single stream for scoring. 2) Sliding-window divergence metric: compute cohort-weighted divergence over a configurable time window (default 10m) with an uncertainty estimate. 3) Per-prompt explainability: surface token-level diffs, hallucination flags, and heuristic categories (e.g., missing facts, truncation, format violation) to speed debugging. 4) Policy integration: configurable actions (alert, pause canary traffic, roll back, escalate to human) per-customer and per-route. 5) Calibration and learning: support automatic threshold calibration using historical rollout data and low-cost synthetic perturbations to reduce false positives.

Trade-offs and considerations: - Cost: real-time scoring of golden sets at canary scale increases token processing and storage costs. We'll mitigate by sampling and adaptive probe frequency. - False positives: explainability and cohort weighting aim to reduce noisy triggers; critical customers will default to human approval. - Latency: scoring is asynchronous and should not add to request latency; however, routing decisions are eventually consistent.

Implementation outline: (a) scoring service that accepts probe results and reference outputs, computes per-probe scores and diffs, and emits aggregate signals to the rollout conductor; (b) Watchtower policy engine that evaluates signals against per-entity policies; (c) Console UI for inspectors and drilldowns; (d) orchestration hooks to canary conductor to pause/quarantine or trigger rollback.

Success metrics (initial): - Precision of watchtower alerts >= 85% on historical simulated regressions. - Mean time to detect regression in canary < 5 minutes for injected degradations. - Reduction in customer-facing rollbacks caused by late-detected regressions by 60% in first quarter of rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring service ingests golden and live probe outputs and produces per-prompt divergence scores within 30s of probe completion
Aggregate divergence computed with cohort-weighting and uncertainty estimation visible in Console for active canaries
Policy engine supports at least three actions: alert (Slack + Console), pause/quarantine canary, initiate rollback workflow to orchestration service
Explainability panel in Console shows top 10 offending prompts with token-level diffs and heuristic labels
Integration tests that inject synthetic regressions into a staging rollout and verify correct policy action are added and green
Documentation and runbook for incident response and threshold tuning published in Confluence
comments: 2026-02-12 Ava Chen: Kickoff — scoped first PoC to scoring service + Console visualization. Identified two main risks: false positives and cost. Decided adaptive sampling to start.

2026-02-20 Mateo Ruiz: Implemented initial scoring prototype; uses BLEU-like and embedding-distance metrics plus a delta baseline. Pushed draft PR for internal review: https://github.com/redwood/watchtower/pull/9
2026-02-25 Design review (J. Patel): Requested clearer UX for explainability panel; suggested category filters and direct links to related PRs and prompts. Adding to UI scope.
2026-03-02 Eng review (S. Gomez): Raised concern about per-token diff compute cost. Decided to persist only diffs for top-N prompts and compute full diffs on demand.
2026-03-08 QA (L. Martinez): Ran simulation harness with 120 historical rollouts; initial alert precision 78%. Working on threshold tuning and cohort weighting. Set next milestone for +85% precision.

2026-03-14 Mateo Ruiz: Merged scoring engine skeleton to staging branch. Console prototype available at /console/watchtower (internal). Next: policy engine and orchestration hook PoC. Linked infra ticket for scaling: ENG-678901
rollout_plan: Week 1: Deploy scoring service to staging, run replay of last 6 months of canary traffic against golden sets
Week 2: Enable Console debug UI and run internal demo; collect feedback and tune heuristics
Week 3: Pilot in production for 5% of canary traffic with alert-only mode for two low-risk services
Week 4: Enable quarantine action for non-critical routes and auto-rollback for synthetic-testing traffic only
Week 5+: Gradually increase coverage and enable customer-specific policies for enterprise customers with human approval gating
test_plan: Add synthetic regression injector to staging orchestration to produce controlled hallucination/missing-fact regressions
Create end-to-end test that validates scoring -> policy engine -> orchestrator pause/rollback path
Create load test for scoring service that simulates 10K probe evaluations per minute and measure cost/latency
User acceptance test with platform reliability team to verify Console explainability workflows
